assessor: Assistant editorial assessment of actual complete Gemini output; not generator self-score or independent blinded human review

evidence.hlni: The real management-title overlap corrects the student’s accounting-only assumption. Programme names/cohort are supported in metadata and cohort is visible, but exact specialisation names should be held clearly in source footage.
evidence.differentiation: A scoped document reveal and a corrected shortlist serve the Trust objective. This rating does not substitute for testing other fresh channels.
evidence.coherence: The student crosses out B.Com, sees the verified management row, then removes the same cross-out. Each stage advances that one causal correction.
evidence.payoff: Shot 5 visibly restores the excluded option for further comparison. It demonstrates the consequence without selecting a degree or claiming equal teaching.
evidence.production: Six shootable scenes, concrete props, concise dialogue and source rows. Clarify exact programme labels and remove any unspecified extra module entries before filming. No recorded read-aloud was performed.
evidence.originality: The cross-out reversal is effective but familiar rather than highly original.

assessments.automaticTriggerExplanation: The supplied shared-title row is supported by the inspected sources. No proven material factual error, wholly missing meaningful insight or impossible production instruction was established. Unsupported extrapolations, where present, still require revision; absence of a proven falsehood is not certification.
reasons: This is a Trust-only pilot assessment; it does not establish three-channel differentiation or production approval.
revisions: Hold exact programme names and the cohort visibly on the source inserts.
Show the restored option as provisional and leave unsupplied assessment/depth fields unknown.
Any comparison cells beyond the one inspected row need verification rather than invented module names.

methodology: The full returned storyboard, HLNI, concept spine, production notes and warnings were read. The same assistant implemented and assessed the change. Scores use the unchanged rubric. Channel differentiation here assesses the recognisable Trust experience against the approved channel objectives and archived references; a fresh three-channel group comparison was not performed. No recorded read-aloud or deployed-app test was performed.
runSummary: The coherent human-premise brief returned a complete six-scene pilot. An optional advisory rewrite failed pacing, so the validated initial Draft was retained. This assessment scores the actual retained script, not the rejected rewrite. It passes the 85 floor at 86, but does not meet the above-90 target or constitute application approval.
crossChannelFinding: Only Trust was generated in this run. Other channels were deliberately held back pending repeatable Trust acceptance. Output remains Draft and no model review grants application approval.
nextStep: Check repeatability on identical source and preserve every failure. Keep the 85 overall/4 HLNI/4 differentiation floors and above-90 target unchanged. Do not expand or deploy based on one passing example.
